title: A multicenter prospective randomized controlled trial to test the safety and efficacy of a systematic app-based remote and home-based prehabilitation program in comparison to education only before major surgeries: The LUMOS Study.
summary:
The safety of major surgeries in the abdomen or thorax depends on the individual patient's fitness. It is important to optimize patients before major surgery. To date, it is challenging to implement a structured prehabilitation program into the preoperative course due to a lack of staff and infrastructure at hospitals and additional travel requirements for patients. There is often too little time or there is simply a lack of knowledge about prehabilitation and its elements. 
Apps can be promising and helpful tools. An app can deliver information and function as an educational tool. Apps can also collect and provide individual exercises and can be very interventional. By that, you can perform risk and age-adapted exercising tailored to your personal health and performance status. This can be done in a supervised fashion together with your surgeons.
We developed two apps for this specific phase before major surgeries. One app is the Ready4OP app, which is a simple educational tool that delivers valuable information and will be used in the control arm of the study. The other app is The Prehab App which is a medical device that is not yet certified and prepares patients remotely at home for major surgeries (interventional arm). Both apps may have beneficial effects, that may improve your health before major surgeries. This means that training you in sports, short-term nutritional advice, and mental well-being should bring you home faster and in case you have any complications after surgery, make you fit faster.
conditions: Patients before major surgeries (noncardia thoracic surgery, abdominal surgery (urologic, gynecologic, vascular, visceral), breast surgery

interventions.name: Educational Prehabilitation with the Ready4OP App (Educational Tool): 3 to 6-week interventional aerobic interval training, 3-4 times per week to increase the aerobic capacity.
Control with the Ready4OP App (educational content): information and learning material without specific recommendations to improve health literacy

- Written informed consent
- Willing to participate
- Patients have an Android or iOS-based smartphone
- Patients who are planned for one of the following surgeries as the leading and initial OPS-code are eligible to participate in the LUMOS trial in case of missing contra-indications and exclusions. Exclusion criteria:
- Younger than 18 years
- Currently pregnant or breastfeeding (anamnestically)
- Unable to understand the rationale and the aims of the proposed training program
- Unable to interact with the application
- Patients with an ECOG performance status >3.
- Patients unable to walk, run, step, or cycle.
- Patients with an acute (on chronic) cardiovascular disease
Acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina (acute phase) (I20.0, I21)
Uncontrolled arrhythmias causing symptoms or hemodynamic compromise
Acute myocarditis or pericarditis (I30, I39, I40)
- Suspected dissecting aneurysm
- Uncontrolled acutely decompensated HF (acute pulmonary edema) (J81)
- HR>120 bpm, BP> 180mmHg sys, 120mmHg diastolic
-Patients with an acute (on chronic) pulmonary disease
-Acute pulmonary embolism (I26)
-Resting dyspnea (Frequency>25)
-Exertional dyspnea after less than 2 floors of step walking
-Chest pain when resting
-Severe hypoxemia at rest or acute respiratory failure (J80)
-An acute, non-cardiopulmonary disorder that may affect exercise performance or be aggravated by exercise (such as infection, renal failure, or thyrotoxicosis)
-Mental impairment leading to inability to cooperate
-Patients under guardianship or imprisoned
